spans.text: (The chazzan proclaims our hope that) soon, in our lifetime, the entire world, which Hashem created precisely according to His Will, will recognize Hashem as the Source of all and will see the sanctity, perfection, and purpose of all He has done.

אָמֵן. יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא—(We all enthusiastically respond:) Absolutely correct! May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that all His actions are great and deserving of praise!

יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח—(The chazzan then points out that) in reality, the true greatness and power of Hashem far exceeds any praises that we mere humans could say. And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely correct!

אֲדֹנָי, שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וּפִי יַגִּיד תְּהִלָּתֶךָ—(I am standing here because I do want to daven, create a relationship, and thank You for all the good You do for me—which is sometimes hard to see or understand—and I want to ask You for the help I need. But that does not come easy to me for so many reasons. Therefore, I am asking, please) Hashem, open my lips and help me express myself properly.

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה, אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵינוּ—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything, You control everything, and have taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history starting from the time of the Avos. You are

all-powerful, You shower us with acts of helpful kindness (even though at times it is hard to see that), and everything is Yours. When dealing with us, You take into account the good deeds of our ancestors, and (everything You do for us is in order to) bring Mashiach to us, their descendants, even if we do not deserve it!

מֶלֶךְ חָפֵץ בַּחַיִּים—Please, Hashem, remember us for life; זָכְרֵנוּ לְחַיִּים for You are our King Who desires life; וְכָתְבֵנוּ בְּסֵפֶר הַחַיִּים—for You are our King Who desires life; וְכָתְבֵנוּ בְּסֵפֶר הַחַיִּים—and write us in the book of life; לְמַעַנְךָ אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים—so that we may be able to continue to serve You and live up to our potential.

מֶלֶךְ—You are our King, You have the power to help us through our difficulties, to save us (from our physical and spiritual enemies), and to protect us (from evil). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מָגֵן אַבְרָהָם—You are the Protector of Avraham (and us, his descendants).
אַתָּה גִּבּוֹר לְעוֹלָם—Hashem, Your power and rulership are permanent, You bring about Techiyas Hameisim (since our souls are eternal), and You have unlimited power to save us.

—You take care of us with Your kindness, and with Your great mercy You revive the dead (literally, Techiyas Hameisim, and You also save those who are near physical or spiritual death), You support those who have fallen (physically and spiritually), You heal

the sick (both physically and emotionally ill) and free those in prison (whether in real prisons or trapped in their own sense of limitations), and You keep the covenant You made with our ancestors. There is no other power like You at all; You have total control over our lives and our ultimate salvation. (And that is why we are turning to You and only You with the upcoming requests in our Shemoneh Esrei.)
—There is no one like You, our merciful Father; זוֹכֵר יְצוּרָיו—Who remembers us, His creations, for life; בְּרַחֲמִים—with mercy. לְחַיִּים
—We have total faith that You will perform Techiyas Hameisim. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים—Who performs Techiyas Hameisim.
performs Techiyas Hameisim. (Even though it has not yet happened, we are so sure that it will happen that we say this brachah in the present tense!)

—You, Hashem, are קָדוֹשׁ, separate and far removed from this physical world, and all that we see You do (וְשִׁמְךָ) is beyond our understanding. But we, Bnei Yisrael, are also קְדוֹשִׁים, separate and removed from the values and

the norms of the regular material world (look at the miracle of our survival! And therefore, even though many times what happens to us seems not to make sense)—we, Your people, praise and thank You every day; בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ—the Almighty, the Kadosh One. (During Aseres Yemei Teshuvah say instead: הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ—the King, the Kadosh One.) (If you forgot—see Appendix 12:1)

אַתָּה חוֹנֵן לָאָדָם דַּעַת—Hashem, through Your kindness, You give mankind knowledge, and You teach us mere humans insight. (On Motzaei Shabbos or Yom Tov, add אַתָּה חוּנַנְתָּנוּ.) Please grant us knowledge, understanding, and the intuitive sense to perceive (right from wrong). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָֹה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; חוֹנֵן הַדָּעַת—Who graciously gives (humans) knowledge.

אַתָּה חוֹנַנְתָּנוּ—Through Your kindness You have given us intelligence so that we may study Your Torah, which teaches us how to fulfill Your mitzvos. And You have made a distinction between that which is holy and that which is secular; between light (good) and darkness (evil); between Bnei Yisrael (us, with our special mission) and the nations of the world; and between Shabbos (which infuses us with kedushah and helps us recharge our neshamos) and the six-day work week (which is now starting, when we must retain that kedushah in a very non-kadosh world). Please, Hashem, let the coming week bring us peace; let it be free of sin; and may we be devoted to Your service.

הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ אָבִינוּ לְתוֹרָתֶךָ—Hashem, our Father, please lead us back to Your Torah; our King, please draw us close to be able to serve You, and help us return to You with sincere and complete teshuvah. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָֹה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הָרוֹצֶה בִּתְשׁוּבָה—Who wants us to do (real and sincere) teshuvah.

—סְלַח לָנוּ אָבִינוּ כִּי חָטָאנוּ Hashem, our Father, please forgive us for we have sinned (through carelessness or weakness); Our King, please pardon us for we have intentionally sinned, because You pardon and forgive. —בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; —חַנּוּן הַמַּרְבֶּה לִסְלֹחַ Who is gracious and forgives us repeatedly.

—רְאֵה נָא בְעָנְיֵנוּ וְרִיבָה רִיבֵנוּ Hashem, look at our suffering, defend our cause, and redeem us soon for the glory of Your Name (because when Bnei Yisrael suffer and are ridiculed, it is a chillul Hashem), for You are a powerful Redeemer. —בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; —גּוֹאֵל יִשְׂרָאֵל Who constantly redeems Bnei Yisrael.

—רְפָאֵנוּ יהוה וְנֵרָפֵא Hashem, please heal us, and then we will be truly healed; —הוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ וְנִוָּשֵׁעָה save us, and then we will be truly saved; —כִּי תְהִלָּתֵנוּ אָתָּה for we understand that the true praise for our recovery is due to You. And bring a complete healing to all our illnesses (physical and emotional).* For You, Hashem, are a faithful and merciful Healer. —בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; —רוֹפֵא חוֹלֵי עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל Who heals the sick of His nation, Bnei Yisrael.

—You, Hashem, Who controls everything, please bless this year and all its types of produce, so that we should be able to enjoy it and use it for good, and give us (in the summer say: a blessing) (in the winter say: rain and dew for a blessing) all over the earth, and may we be satisfied with all the good You give us! And please bless this year like the best of years. —You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; —Who blesses the years.

—Hashem, sound the great shofar for our freedom, and raise up a banner (make a public demonstration of Your Divine Presence) in order to gather all our exiles, and gather us together from the four corners of the earth (to our Land).
—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מְקַבֵּץ נִדְחֵי עַמּוֹ—Who gathers the scattered of His nation, Bnei Yisrael.

—Restore our judges and those who guide us, as in earlier times, and remove from us sorrow and worry and confusion, and may You, Hashem alone, rule over us and guide us with kindness and compassion and vindicate us in our judgment. —You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מֶלֶךְ אוֹהֵב צְדָקָה—the King Who loves righteousness and justice. (During Aseres Yemei Teshuvah say instead: הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט—the King of justice.) (If you made a mistake, see Appendix 12:5)

And for those who slander (Bnei Yisrael), let there be no hope; and may all evil instantly be destroyed; and may all Your enemies and the enemies of Your nation be quickly cut down; and may You speedily uproot, crush, cast down, and humble all the arrogant, insolent, and intentional sinners swiftly in our days. בָּרוּךְ
—שׁוֹבֵר אוֹיְבִים וּמַכְנִיעַ זֵדִים; אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; Who destroys enemies and humbles the arrogant and the intentional sinners.

You, Hashem, Who controls everything, may Your mercy be aroused on all the tzaddikim; and on all the elders and leaders of Your nation, Bnei Yisrael; and also on all the righteous converts; and also on us! וְתֵן שָׂכָר And—טוֹב לְכָל הַבּוֹטְחִים בְּשִׁמְךָ בֶּאֱמֶת grant great reward to all who sincerely trust in You, and include us (who sometimes struggle with our bitachon) together with all of them; וְלֹא נֵבוֹשׁ כִּי בְךָ בָּטָחְנוּ—and may we never feel embarrassed (to do the right thing), for we put our trust in You! בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מִשְׁעָן וּמִבְטָח לַצַּדִּיקִים—Who is the support and Source of trust for the tzaddikim.

—וְלִירוּשָׁלַיִם עִירְךָ בְּרַחֲמִים תָּשׁוּב Hashem, even if we are not deserving, please return to Your city of Yerushalayim; and let Your Presence be felt there as You have promised; and rebuild it (the city and the Beis Hamikdash) soon,

in our days, as an everlasting structure; and please (speedily) reestablish within it the throne of David HaMelech. בָּרוּךְ בּוֹנֵה יְהוָה אַתָּה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; יְרוּשָׁלַיִם—Who builds Yerushalayim (present tense—since every step of our galus is a necessary part of the process of the eventual permanent rebuilding of Yerushalayim).

May אֶת צֶמַח דָּוִד עַבְדְּךָ—May Mashiach speedily appear; and may his power and glory be recognized by all thanks to Your salvation, for we await and hope for Your salvation all day and every day. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה
יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מַצְמִיחַ קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה—Who makes the power and glory of our salvation appear (present tense—just like the previous brachah).

שְׁמַע קוֹלֵנוּ—You, Hashem, Who controls everything, please listen to our voice, spare us, and have compassion on us; and accept our tefillos with mercy (if we are not really deserving); and with favor (if we are deserving); for You, Hashem, listen to tefillos and pleadings. וּמִלְּפָנֶיךָ מַלְכֵּנוּ רֵיקָם אַל תְּשִׁיבֵנוּ—Do not turn us away empty-handed from You, our King!

(Now stop for a second. Here is your big chance! This is where you may add any and all personal requests you have! Whatever is in your heart and on your mind, don't be shy to speak it out now, Hashem understands all languages and He listens!)

כִּי אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ—For You, Hashem, listen with compassion to the tefillos of Your nation Bnei Yisrael (including me!). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה—Who listens to tefillah.

רְצֵה יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל—You, Hashem, Who controls everything, be pleased with Your nation Bnei Yisrael and listen to their tefillos; וְהָשֵׁב אֶת—and bring back הָעֲבוֹדָה לִדְבִיר בֵּיתֶךָ—the avodah in the Beis Hamikdash, and please accept their tefillos with love and favor, and all the mitzvos of Bnei Yisrael should always be favorable and acceptable to You.

אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ—Hashem, Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history, please view us favorably, and take into account our special relationship with You and the promises You made to our ancestors: the promise to bring Mashiach and to rebuild Yerushalayim and restore its holiness, and to remember all of Bnei Yisrael everywhere, to deliver us from our exiles (physical and spiritual), and to grant our requests and have mercy on us

(even if we are not deserving), and to give us all life and peace on this day of: Rosh Chodesh/Pesach/Sukkos. Give us all goodness, blessings, and life (even if we are not all deserving), show compassion on us, because we have turned to You for help, because we know that You, Hashem, control everything, and You are a compassionate and merciful King.
You are the benevolent One, for Your compassion is never-ending; You are the merciful One, for Your loving-kindness is never exhausted. From the beginning of time, we have placed our hope in You.

(וְ)—We also thank You) for our miraculous rescue, for the mighty acts and victories, and for the battles (from which You allowed us to emerge victorious) that You performed for our ancestors in those days at this season.

In—בִּימֵי מַתִּתְיָהוּ On Chanukah: the days of the Kohen Gadol Matisyahu the Chashmonai and his children, the despotic Syrian-Greek empire rose up against Your people (Bnei Yisrael), to try to make them forget Your Torah and abandon the Torah way of life. But You, in Your great mercy, stood by the Torah-true Jews in their time of distress and championed their cause, defended their rights, and avenged the wrongs done to them. You made the weak and few (army of the Chashmonaim) victorious

over the stronger and more numerous (Greek army). You made the Jews who had remained pure from the immorality of the Greek culture (טְהוֹרִים), who had remained righteous and loyal to Torah standards (צַדִּיקִים), and who remained diligent in the study of Torah (עוֹסְקֵי תּוֹרָתֶךָ) victorious over the Jews who had taken the side of the Greeks, adopted the immorality of Greek culture (טְמֵאִים and רְשָׁעִים), and deliberately tried to eradicate Torah study (זֵדִים). All the world recognized Your power and greatness, and You brought about a great liberating victory for Your nation. Then Your children cleaned up and purified the Beis Hamikdash and lit the Menorah and instituted these eight days of Chanukah for giving thanks and praise to You.

In—בִּימֵי מָרְדְּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר On Purim: the days of Mordechai and Esther, in the capital city of Shushan, the evil Haman rose up to exterminate all Jews, young and old, on the thirteenth day of Adar. But You in Your great mercy thwarted his plan and caused his scheme against us to boomerang
onto his own head, and he and his sons were hung on the gallows.

וְעַל כֻּלָּם—Our King, for all these things may Your Name be blessed and held in the highest esteem (may everyone realize that You alone are the Source of hidden miracles and loving-kindness), constantly, forever and ever.
וּכְתֹב לְחַיִּים טוֹבִים—And may all the children of Your covenant with the Avos (that's us!) be written for a good life.

וְכֹל הַחַיִּים—And all that live will thank You forever; וִיהַלְלוּ—and sincerely praise all that You do; הָאֵל יְשׁוּעָתֵנוּ—You are our salvation and everlasting help. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הַטּוֹב שִׁמְךָ וּלְךָ נָאֶה—לְהוֹדוֹת—Your very essence is goodness and benevolence, and therefore it is (always) fitting to thank You (in all circumstances of our lives, even if we cannot see the good at the moment).

שָׁלוֹם רָב—Hashem, grant abundant (inner and communal) peace upon Your nation Bnei Yisrael forever, for You are the Master of peace. And may it be favorable in Your eyes to bless Your people, Bnei Yisrael, at all times and at every moment, with Your peace (protection from wars and dangers).
בְּסֵפֶר חַיִּים—May we and Your entire nation, the family of Bnei Yisrael, be remembered and written in the book of life, brachah, peace, and prosperity, for a good life and for peace.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הַמְבָרֵךְ אֶת הַמְבָרֵךְ אֶת—Who blesses His people, Bnei Yisrael, with (all forms of) peace.
יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי—May all that I have said (during this Shemoneh Esrei) and all the thoughts in my heart be acceptable to You, Hashem, my rock and my redeemer.

אֱלֹהַי—Please, Hashem, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking with dishonesty. And to those who curse or insult me, let me have the ability to remain silent and not respond. Open my heart to Your Torah so that my neshamah will desire and run after mitzvos. And all those who plot evil against me, Hashem, please nullify and thwart their plans.

מִלְּפָנֶיךָ—Please, Hashem, let no one be jealous of me, and may I not be jealous of others. Do not allow the yetzer hara to get the better of me, and help me stay humble (despite my accomplishments today) and not be arrogant. Please rebuild the Beis Hamikdash so that the whole world will recognize Your providence, and bring us all back to Yerushalayim.

עֲשֵׂה לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ—Even though I may personally not be worthy, do this for the sake of Your holy Name and for the honor of Your Torah, because we are Your beloved children; therefore with strength and power save me and answer my requests. יִהְיוּ לִרְצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי—May all that I have said (during this Shemoneh Esrei) and all the thoughts in my heart be acceptable to You, Hashem, my rock and my redeemer.

עֹשֶׂה הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו—May He Who makes peace in the Heavens (in the world of angels and in nature); הוּא יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ—may He bring about peace upon us (since we seem to have a hard time doing it ourselves, may Hashem impose peace upon us!); וְעַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל—and upon all of Bnei Yisrael; וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן—and (may the two angels who accompany me through life and therefore have been listening to my tefillah, please respond and) say Amen.
May it be Your will, Hashem, Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history, that the Beis Hamikdash be rebuilt quickly in our days, and help us find

our unique connection to Your Torah. And there (in the Beis Hamikdash) we will be able to serve You with proper respect, as it was in the days of old. (And when Mashiach arrives and rebuilds the Beis Hamikdash) then the korbanos of Yehudah and Yerushalayim will be accepted by Hashem, as it was in the days of old.

(The chazzan proclaims our hope that) soon, in our lifetime, the entire world, which Hashem created precisely according to His Will, will recognize Hashem as the Source of all and will see the sanctity, perfection, and purpose of all He has done.

אָמֵן. יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא—(We all enthusiastically respond:) Absolutely correct! May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that all His actions are great and deserving of praise!

FAQ:
Why am I asking Hashem for stuff? Hashem knows what I want, and He also knows what I really need! If I really need it and am supposed to have it, He would have given it to me!

FAQ:
Why should I bother making requests from Hashem? I've asked Him many times before for stuff, and He keeps on saying no!

ANSWER:
Both very crucial questions for a serious Ben Torah and Bas Yisrael! See Appendix 1.

The terms מוֹשִׁיעַ, עוֹזֵר and מָגֵן represent three levels of help that we need in our lives—from the least to the most. עוֹזֵר—"help," is when we are on the right track, doing what we need to do in the best way possible, and we ask Hashem to please help us that all should work out, since nothing will come to fruition without His help. מוֹשִׁיעַ—"salvation," is when we are completely at a loss; we throw up our hands and say to Hashem, "Save me, I have no idea what to do next!" The third and highest level, מָגֵן—"protect," is when we think we're on the right track and think we know what we're doing, but in truth we are completely off base! We ask Hashem, "If I'm going in the wrong direction—מָגֵן—protect me from myself!"
During Aseres Yemei Teshuvah add: (If you forgot—see Appendix 12:1)
During the winter add:
In Israel in the summer add:
(If you made a mistake—see Appendix 12:3)
During Aseres Yemei Teshuvah add: (If you forgot—see Appendix 12:1)
Help me understand
On Motzaei Shabbos or Yom Tov add the following:

(Continue: Please grant us knowledge…)
(If you forgot to add, do not go back or repeat Shemoneh Esrei.)
Help me get close to You
FAQ: But I keep on messing up! Maybe I should just give up. I've tried so many times to do the right thing, and yet I keep on failing!
ANSWER: Good question! Everyone feels that way sometimes—including me! See Appendix 3.

spans.text: יש אומרים כאן תפילה זו:

Why do we say "listen to our voice (קולנו)"? Shouldn't we ask Hashem to listen to the words we say? What we are asking Hashem is: "I may not be so articulate and may not know how to say what I really feel. But I hope You can tell from the sound of my voice that I am doing the best I can to communicate with You!"

We asked Hashem to "accept our tefillos," so what are we adding by requesting, "Do not turn us away empty-handed"? Of course, we hope that Hashem will grant us what we have requested, but sometimes, for reasons known only to Him, Hashem must say no. We therefore ask Hashem that if the answer to our tefillah must be a no, then at least do not send us away feeling "empty-handed"—with a feeling of total rejection. Let our hearts be filled with emunah that we had the amazing zechus and opportunity to talk one-on-one with Hashem and He heard our tefillah, even if the best thing for us right now is a no.
